biz: Designs and manufactures transformers, inductors and wound components — 25VA to 35kVA standard, bespoke to 500kVA — plus power supplies, LED drivers and thermal management. Family-run, established 1984.
why: A UL-listed transformer manufacturer with ISO 9001/14001 and MoD, Ford and Scottish Power on the client list — presenting itself as a Mean Well reseller with a shopping basket. That mismatch is exactly what Aster fixes, and it maps directly onto the Power Tagun work.
good: They are genuinely transacting online — live ex-VAT pricing, stock indicators, downloadable catalogues, WorldPay checkout. Most manufacturers of this age never got e-commerce working at all.
prob: Authorised-distributor badges sit above the fold and the product tiles read as catalogue resale, so a first-time visitor concludes ETE distributes other people's transformers. The in-house manufacturing story — UL listing, bespoke 500kVA capability, 42-year history, blue-chip clients — appears nowhere on the homepage. No case studies, no testimonials, no named team on the main site despite a full leadership page existing.

biz: Manufactures custom special bolting and high-integrity fasteners in exotic materials — Monel, Hastelloy, Inconel — in small-to-medium batches for nuclear, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and renewable energy. Founded 1971.
why: A third-generation family manufacturer certified for nuclear and pressure-equipment work, with a genuinely compelling 55-year story — and a website that buries all of it under technical density. good: The technical content operation is unusually good for a firm this size — thirteen downloadable technical sheets, PDF guides, a client download portal, UKAS-approved lab testing across seventeen-plus categories, and BS EN 10204:2004 certification at multiple levels. They have already done the hard work of being genuinely useful to engineers.
prob: Mid-to-late-2010s corporate WordPress — functional but visually dated. Dense text blocks with minimal breathing room, oversized certificate thumbnails dominating the whitespace, dated banner styling, and a comprehensive but heavy navigation creating real cognitive load. The consequential gap: no one from the company is visible anywhere on the front end — no leadership, no faces, no named engineers — despite the business's single strongest differentiator being three generations of the same family. The 2017 BBC Breakfast feature is on the site but reads as archival rather than as proof.
